name: Ashbel
title: Son of Benjamin and ancestor of the Ashbelites
summary: Asbel was the son of Benjamin and grandson of the patriarch Jacob and Rachel. He is mentioned in the genealogies in Genesis, Numbers, and 1 Chronicles as part of the generation of Jacob's family that went to Egypt during the famine. Asbel became the ancestor of the Asbelites, one of the recognized clans within the tribe of Benjamin. Notably, Asbel is among the few names that appear consistently across all three biblical genealogical records of Benjamin's sons, even though these lists otherwise vary significantly in both the names included and their total number. This testifies to the fact that Asbel's clan held a stable and important position within the tribe of Benjamin through several periods of Israel's history.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in Jacob's family that went to Egypt
keyEvents.description: Ashbel is listed among the sons of Benjamin who were part of Jacob's family when they went down to Egypt during the famine.

keyEvents.title: Registered in Israel's census
keyEvents.description: In the census on the plains of Moab, Ashbel's clan is mentioned as part of the tribe of Benjamin, known as the Ashbelites.

keyEvents.title: Listed in Benjamin's genealogy in Chronicles
keyEvents.description: Ashbel is included in the genealogy of Benjamin's descendants in 1 Chronicles, where he is named as Benjamin's second son, after Bela.

versions.summary: Ashbel was the second son of Benjamin, who in turn was the youngest son of the patriarch Jacob. He is mentioned in the genealogies in Genesis, Numbers, and 1 Chronicles as part of Benjamin's descendants who went down to Egypt. As a forefather of one of the clans in the tribe of Benjamin, he played a role in Israel's tribal history.
versions.title: Son of Benjamin
versions.reason: [minor] The role 'patriarch' may be somewhat misleading for Ashbel. He was a forefather of a clan in the tribe of Benjamin, but the term 'patriarch' is usually used concerning Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. 'Forefather' or 'clan founder' would have been more precise.; [major] The names of Benjamin's sons in Gen 46:21 vary somewhat between different textual witnesses, but the common Norwegian forms include among others Bela, Becher, Ashbel, Gera, Naaman, Ehi, Rosh, Muppim, Huppim and Ard. 'Akra' is not a recognizable form – this should be 'Becher'. 'Noman' should probably be 'Naaman'.; [minor] The summary states that Ashbel was 'the second son of Benjamin'. In Gen 46:21 the order is Bela, Becher, Ashbel – thus Ashbel is the third, not the second son mentioned. In 1 Chr 8:1 he is indeed mentioned as the second. It should be formulated more neutrally to avoid contradiction between the sources.; [minor] The fourth key event ('Part of Jacob's family of 70 persons') overlaps thematically with the first event. This gives some redundancy. They could possibly be merged, but it is not critical.; [minor] Footnotes are missing. Notes should be added concerning name variations between Gen 46, Num 26 and 1 Chr 8, as well as about the possible meaning of the name.; [minor] 'Ehi' should probably be written 'Eki' or similar depending on Norwegian tradition. The name varies between textual witnesses. In 1 Chr 8:1 Ashbel is mentioned as number two, and the list of siblings is different from Gen 46:21.

versions.summary: Asbel was one of the sons of Benjamin, who in turn was the youngest son of the patriarch Jacob. He is mentioned in the genealogies in Genesis, Numbers and 1 Chronicles as part of Benjamin's descendants who went down to Egypt. As the ancestor of the Asbelites – one of the clans within the tribe of Benjamin – he played a role in Israel's tribal history. His name appears consistently in the various family records, indicating that his clan was an established part of the tribe of Benjamin through several generations.
versions.title: Son of Benjamin and ancestor of the Ashbelites
versions.reason: [minor] The fourth key event element ('Part of Jacob's family that came to Egypt') overlaps thematically strongly with the first ('Mentioned in Jacob's lineage as those who went to Egypt'). Both concern the journey to Egypt. The fourth element refers to Gen 46:26-27, which is a summary of the number of people, not a specific mention of Ashbel. Consider merging these or removing the fourth event to avoid redundancy.; [minor] In 1 Chr 8:1, Ashbel is mentioned as the second son, but in some manuscripts and translations the order differs slightly. The description 'where he is mentioned as the second son' is essentially correct according to 1 Chr 8:1, but it should be phrased somewhat more cautiously.; [minor] The wording 'who again was the youngest son of the patriarch Jacob' is somewhat imprecise. Benjamin is traditionally regarded as Jacob's youngest son, but strictly speaking he was the youngest of Rachel's sons and Jacob's second-youngest in chronological terms (his position depends on whether we count the sons of the handmaids). The wording should be clarified.; [minor] The roles 'patriarch' and 'founder' are very overlapping. Consider replacing with, for example, 'ancestor of the Ashbelites' or adding 'son of Benjamin' as a role for more variety.

versions.summary: Asbel was one of the sons of Benjamin, Jacob's youngest son with Rachel. He is mentioned in the genealogies in Genesis, Numbers and 1 Chronicles, and belonged to the generation of Jacob's family that went down to Egypt during the great famine. Asbel became the ancestor of the Asbelites, one of the recognized clans within the tribe of Benjamin. It is noteworthy that his name appears in all three biblical genealogical records of Benjamin's sons, even though these lists otherwise vary considerably in the names included and their numbers. This suggests that Asbel's clan held a stable and established position within the tribe of Benjamin through several centuries of Israel's history.
versions.title: Son of Benjamin and ancestor of the Ashbelites
versions.reason: [minor] The list of siblings in Gen 46:21 includes ten names, but the lists vary among biblical sources. The listed siblings match Gen 46:21, though it may be worth noting that some of these names (such as Naaman and Ard) are counted as grandchildren rather than sons in other texts. Nevertheless, the list is acceptable as it stands, since it follows the most detailed source.; [minor] The description states that Ashbel is mentioned 'among the first sons' in 1 Chr 8:1. In this text, he is actually named second – after Bela. The wording is not directly incorrect, but could be clarified somewhat.

footnotes.text: The name Ashbel (Hebrew: אַשְׁבֵּל) has an uncertain etymology. Some scholars suggest the meaning 'God's fire' (from 'esh' = fire + 'el' = God), while others believe it may mean 'man of Baal' or that it has another Semitic root. The exact meaning is debated.

The lists of Benjamin's sons vary significantly between Gen 46:21 (ten sons), Num 26:38–41 (five sons), and 1 Chron 8:1–2 (five sons). Ashbel is one of the few who appears consistently in all three lists, indicating that he was an important forefather in the tribe of Benjamin.

The differences in the genealogical lists may reflect that some named 'sons' were actually grandchildren or clan names, and that the lists were compiled at different times for various purposes – genealogical, administrative, or cultic.

The tribe of Benjamin, to which the clan of Ashbel belonged, played an important role in Israel's later history. The tribe gave Israel its first king, Saul, and was known for its skilled archers and slingers (Judg 20:16). The Ashbelites were part of this tribal identity.

The Septuagint (the Greek translation of the Old Testament) renders the name Ashbel as Ἀσβήλ (Asbēl). In some Greek manuscripts, there are minor variations in spelling, which indicates uncertainty about the precise pronunciation already in antiquity.
